newsitem.title: USA: Pilots adjourn AMR talks, to resume on Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Pilots adjourn AMR talks, to resume on Saturday.

text.p: The pilots union board met for five hours on Friday to weigh a new contract with American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp., and is to resume deliberation on Saturday, pilot spokesman Wally Pitts said.

He said the 18-member board was briefed by its negotiating team on American's offer in the morning and later the team worked with airline officials to put into contractual language the agreement in principle reached on Wednesday.

The pact, to resolve the Allied Pilots Association's three-year labor dispute with American, covers pay and who is to fly the new, small regional jets American plans to buy for it commuter airline, American Eagle.

Eagle's turbo fleet is flown by members of the Air Line Pilots Association, who are paid on average one-third of the $120,000 a year earned by APA's pilots. APA pilots want to be in the cockpit of the new jets.
Officials said they thought it likely the board would complete its deliberations on Saturday and vote on whether or not to accept American's proposal.
If accepted, the proposal would be sent to the union's 9,300 pilots for ratification. The union has threatened to go on strike on April 28 if no new contract is reached.
